concepts.name: Kamala Nehru's Entry into Active Politics: Transition from Private to Public Life
key_dimensions: Circumstances of her politicization — influence of Non-Cooperation Movement (1920–22) vs. personal conviction
Contrast with her initial domestic, apolitical role in the Nehru household
Role of Jawaharlal Nehru's imprisonment as a catalyst for her independent activism
UPSC trap: distinguishing her autonomous political identity from being merely an extension of Nehru family politics

concepts.name: Kamala Nehru's Role in the Civil Disobedience Movement (1930–32)
key_dimensions: Leadership of picketing campaigns against liquor and foreign cloth shops in Allahabad
Organizing women volunteers independently — significance of women-led local units
Her arrest in 1930 and the political symbolism of a woman from the elite Nehru family courting imprisonment
Comparison with other women leaders arrested during CDM (e.g., Sarojini Naidu, Aruna Asaf Ali)

concepts.name: Kamala Nehru's Illness and Political Continuity: Activism Despite Tuberculosis
key_dimensions: Timeline of her illness vis-à-vis her active political engagements — often tested for contradiction
Her participation in the 1932 Individual Satyagraha despite deteriorating health
The political and personal significance of her death in Lausanne (1936) — impact on Nehru and the nationalist movement
UPSC trap: her death is sometimes conflated with the timeline of the 1937 elections or Congress's internal politics

concepts.name: Kamala Nehru and the Constructive Programme: Grassroots Mobilization
key_dimensions: Her work in promoting khadi and village industries in the United Provinces
Role in mobilizing women from conservative Hindu households into nationalist activities
Connection between Gandhian constructive programme and women's political empowerment
Distinction between her constructive work and the more confrontational satyagraha roles

concepts.name: Kasturba Gandhi's Evolution: From Obedient Wife to Independent Nationalist Icon
key_dimensions: Early resistance to Gandhi's demands (e.g., cleaning latrines episode in South Africa) — asserting personal dignity
Transition from passive compliance to active co-leadership in South Africa (1913 Satyagraha)
Her independent moral authority among women and rural masses in India
UPSC trap: distinguishing her as an autonomous political actor vs. merely following Gandhi's directives

concepts.name: Kasturba Gandhi in South Africa: The 1913 Natal Satyagraha
key_dimensions: Her role in leading a march of indentured workers from Natal into Transvaal — crossing provincial borders as an act of resistance
Arrest, imprisonment, and the political fallout — galvanizing Indian opinion both in South Africa and India
Significance of a woman leading a workers' march in the context of early 20th-century gender norms
Comparison with other women's roles in the South African passive resistance movement

concepts.name: Kasturba Gandhi and the Champaran Satyagraha (1917): Women's Mobilization in Agrarian Struggle
key_dimensions: Her specific role in educating and organizing women in Champaran villages — sanitation, literacy, health
Constructive programme work as a tool of political consciousness-raising among peasant women
Champaran as the first major instance of Gandhi-Kasturba joint mobilization on Indian soil
UPSC trap: Champaran is primarily associated with Gandhi — her distinct contribution is frequently overlooked

concepts.name: Kasturba Gandhi's Arrests and Imprisonments in India: The Rajkot and Quit India Episodes
key_dimensions: Rajkot Satyagraha (1939) — her independent courting of arrest when Gandhi was barred from continuing
Arrest during the Quit India Movement (1942) — imprisoned at Aga Khan Palace, Pune
Her death in detention (February 22, 1944) — political and symbolic significance for the nationalist movement
UPSC trap: confusing the location of her death (Aga Khan Palace) with other Gandhi-related detention sites

concepts.name: Kasturba Gandhi's Death in Detention (1944): Political Symbolism and Nationalist Response
key_dimensions: Impact of her death on public sentiment during the Quit India Movement
British government's handling of her death — criticism and political embarrassment for colonial administration
Gandhi's response and the transformation of her image into a nationalist martyr
Comparison with deaths of other nationalist figures in custody and their political consequences

concepts.name: Comparative Roles: Kamala Nehru vs. Kasturba Gandhi — Scope and Style of Activism
key_dimensions: Urban elite mobilization (Kamala) vs. rural and cross-class mobilization (Kasturba)
Kamala's focus on direct political confrontation (picketing, satyagraha) vs. Kasturba's blend of constructive work and direct action
Both defined by the tension between personal relationships with dominant nationalist husbands and independent political identities
UPSC trap: questions that ask which of the two had a 'larger' political role — requires nuanced answer based on context

concepts.name: Kasturba Gandhi's Role in Ashram Life and Women's Empowerment: Sabarmati and Sevagram
key_dimensions: Ashrams as training grounds for women's political and social participation
Kasturba's role in managing ashram discipline, women's quarters, and practical education
The ashram model as an alternative space for women outside traditional domestic roles
Connection between ashram constructive work (spinning, weaving) and the larger Swadeshi political economy

concepts.name: Kamala Nehru and Congress Women's Organizations: Institutional Role
key_dimensions: Her involvement with the All India Congress Committee's women's wings and local Pradesh Congress committees
Significance of women organizing within Congress vs. separate women's organizations (e.g., All India Women's Conference)
Her role in legitimizing middle-class and upper-class women's political participation within mainstream Congress
UPSC trap: distinguishing Congress-affiliated women's activism from autonomous women's organizations of the period

concepts.name: The 'Nationalist Wife' Paradigm and Its Subversion by Kamala and Kasturba
key_dimensions: How the dominant nationalist narrative instrumentalized women as supportive figures — and how both women exceeded this role
Instances where both women acted against or beyond the wishes of their husbands (Kasturba's early resistance; Kamala's independent political decisions)
Historiographical debate: feminist historians vs. mainstream nationalist historians on the agency of these women
Relevance to broader UPSC theme of women's agency in the freedom struggle

concepts.name: Kasturba Gandhi's Religious and Social Reform Activities: Caste and Untouchability
key_dimensions: Her initial resistance to Gandhi's insistence on admitting untouchables into the ashram — and her eventual acceptance
Role in the anti-untouchability campaigns alongside Gandhi's Harijan movement
The tension between her orthodox Hindu upbringing and the reformist demands of nationalist politics
UPSC trap: her initial resistance is sometimes used to mischaracterize her overall social outlook

concepts.name: Kamala Nehru's International Profile: Visit to Europe and Political Significance
key_dimensions: Her travels to Europe for medical treatment (1935–36) and simultaneous political engagements
Meetings with European socialists and anti-imperialists — internationalizing the Indian freedom struggle
The intersection of her personal health crisis with her political visibility abroad
Contrast with other Indian women who represented the nationalist cause internationally (e.g., Vijayalakshmi Pandit, Sarojini Naidu)

concepts.name: Women's Participation in the Quit India Movement (1942): Kasturba as Symbol
key_dimensions: Kasturba's planned speech at Shivaji Park (Mumbai) before her arrest — the act of attempting to speak as a political act
Her role as a symbol for thousands of women who participated in the Quit India Movement
The Quit India Movement as the highpoint of mass women's participation in the freedom struggle
UPSC trap: distinguishing between women who led the movement (Aruna Asaf Ali going underground) vs. Kasturba's symbolic martyrdom through imprisonment

concepts.name: Kasturba Gandhi Trust and Post-Independence Legacy of Kasturba's Work
key_dimensions: Establishment of Kasturba Gandhi National Memorial Trust (1945) — objectives and founding context
Focus on rural women's education and welfare — continuity with her ashram and constructive programme work
Gandhi's role in institutionalizing her legacy immediately after her death
UPSC relevance: connecting her legacy to post-independence women's welfare schemes and Gandhian institutions

concepts.name: Historiographical Framing: Recovery of Kamala and Kasturba from Nationalist Footnotes
key_dimensions: Mainstream nationalist historiography's tendency to subsume their roles under Gandhi's and Nehru's biographies
Feminist historiography (e.g., Geraldine Forbes, Aparna Basu) recovering their independent political agency
The problem of sources: their voices are primarily mediated through husbands' autobiographies (Discovery of India, Gandhi's autobiography)
UPSC relevance: 'critically examine' questions on women's roles in the freedom struggle require this historiographical awareness

concepts.name: Intersection of Gender, Class, and Nationalism: Kamala and Kasturba as Case Studies
key_dimensions: Both women came from relatively privileged backgrounds yet engaged with mass politics — class dimensions of their activism
How caste and class shaped the scope of their outreach (Kasturba's broader rural reach vs. Kamala's urban constituency)
The gendered constraints both faced — health, domesticity, lack of formal education — and how they navigated them
Relevance to UPSC theme: 'Women's participation in the freedom struggle was shaped as much by social structures as by political ideology'

concepts.name: Kamala Nehru and Indira Gandhi: Intergenerational Transfer of Political Identity
key_dimensions: Kamala's influence on the young Indira Gandhi's nationalist consciousness — Indira's participation in Vanar Sena
Indira's public statements on her mother's political courage as a formative influence
The significance of Kamala's independent activism for Indira's later political self-fashioning
UPSC trap: questions linking Indira Gandhi's political entry to Nehru family legacy often omit Kamala's specific influence
